title: Triangle
prompt: Given a `triangle` array of arrays representing a triangular arrangement of numbers, return the minimum path sum from top to bottom. At each step you may move to an adjacent number on the row below, meaning from index `i` on the current row you can move to index `i` or index `i + 1` on the next row.

examples.explanation: With just two rows, the only choices from the top are 2 or 3, and 1+2=3 is the minimum.

hints: Working top-down means each cell has a variable number of valid predecessors depending on position — working bottom-up avoids that edge-case juggling entirely.
Start from the bottom row as your base case, then repeatedly collapse each row into the row above it using the best of the two adjacent choices below.
dp[i] = triangle[row][i] + min(dp[i], dp[i+1]), updating a single array in place as you move upward row by row; the final answer ends up at dp[0].

solution.approach: Work from the bottom of the triangle upward instead of top-down, since every cell in the bottom row is trivially a base case (the path sum starting there is just its own value), and it avoids special-casing edges on the top-down version. Initialize dp as a copy of the last row. Then for each row moving upward, update dp[i] = triangle[row][i] + min(dp[i], dp[i+1]) — this represents choosing the cheaper of the two reachable cells directly below. After processing row 0, dp[0] holds the minimum total path sum from top to bottom.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) where n is the number of rows
